While I just spent several paragraphs, talk about the importance of internal, locus of control, and embracing the belief, you determine your trading outcomes. There's 1 extremely important, external factor to consider, you cannot succeed in an unhealthy trading environment. You must have a risk-taking environment that's not hostile to risk or thinly capitalized. This point could have been at the top of this chapter, because in the wrong environment, even the most rational disciplined skilled. And self-aware Trader will fail. There are many features of a trading environment that can be desirable, but there are 2 that are absolutely necessary for survival and success 1, appropriate Capital 2 healthy and supportive risk taking environment. Let's look at each feature separately. Appropriate capital. In terms of external factors sufficient capital is an absolute prerequisite for successful trading. Let's look at what this means for the 3 main types of Trader. Retail Traders. no retail Trader can succeed with the $1,000 trading account because the income generated from the most successful, Strategy will be too small to move the needle. Even a 300% return will not be enough to make a difference. And so the trader is very likely to employ too much leverage and blow up the account by a gambling. A tiny trading account is okay, for learning the markets and much better than paper trading. It might give you a sense of the emotional and psychological hurdles that come with live trading, but it will never give you a chance to really know what kind of Trader you are. In general position, sizing can account for most issues, around insufficient Capital. If your capital is small, you need to take smaller positions and we'll discuss position sizing in Chapter 11. But there are thresholds below, which you cannot hope to succeed. For young retail Trader, with no family to support and low expenses. This amount could be as low as 25,000. For a dentist with 3 kids in private school, looking to quit his job and trade full-time. This number would be significantly higher. Bank Traders.
